investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-24T17:18–17:25Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" appeared identically across all three sibling checks, indicating that no new peer-pod VM slot is available on any schedulable node. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not proceed, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (check-expectations.json line 256) received zero evidence fields.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. A reduction in the eligible node pool (e.g., a node being cordoned, drained, or relabeled) would shrink available capacity to zero.
Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm reached at the namespace or org level, preventing new VM allocations even if node capacity nominally exists.

A surge in concurrent remote agent workloads (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all peer-pod slots before the eval probes ran, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity shortfall.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-24 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a successfully scheduled pod before it can poll state or write any evidence; because scheduling fails, the check times out and produces an empty evidence object, violating all four required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/Kata peer-pods node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes, meaning the resource quota is at or above its limit (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the other 4 nodes in the 6-node cluster do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were freed on those nodes it would not help without affinity changes.

Concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads left pods running without cleanup, the resource pool may be fully occupied. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful and no new nodes were added during the ~145s window, suggesting autoscaling is either absent, slow, or not configured for this node pool.

Node pool sized too small for concurrent eval runs: with only 2 kata-capable nodes and a fixed vm resource limit per node, simultaneous eval probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime ran within the same ~5-minute window) may collectively exhaust capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-24T17:18–17:25Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" appeared identically across all three sibling checks, indicating that no new peer-pod VM slot is available on any schedulable node. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not proceed, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (check-expectations.json line 256) received zero evidence fields.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 128s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck 147s, endedAt 2026-06-24T17:25:36.647Z

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod did not schedule
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. A reduction in the eligible node pool (e.g., a node being cordoned, drained, or relabeled) would shrink available capacity to zero.
Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm reached at the namespace or org level, preventing new VM allocations even if node capacity nominally exists.

A surge in concurrent remote agent workloads (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all peer-pod slots before the eval probes ran, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity shortfall.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-create probe that returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would indicate the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

Cluster node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are currently consuming all slots would rule out resource exhaustion and point instead to a pod spec misconfiguration (wrong node selector, missing toleration, or incorrect resource request).

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for pod scheduling timeout.

Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies at least N nodes carry the required kata.peerpods.io/vm label and are in Ready/schedulable state, alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-24 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a successfully scheduled pod before it can poll state or write any evidence; because scheduling fails, the check times out and produces an empty evidence object, violating all four required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/Kata peer-pods node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes, meaning the resource quota is at or above its limit (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the other 4 nodes in the 6-node cluster do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were freed on those nodes it would not help without affinity changes.

Concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads left pods running without cleanup, the resource pool may be fully occupied. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful and no new nodes were added during the ~145s window, suggesting autoscaling is either absent, slow, or not configured for this node pool.

Node pool sized too small for concurrent eval runs: with only 2 kata-capable nodes and a fixed vm resource limit per node, simultaneous eval probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime ran within the same ~5-minute window) may collectively exhaust capacity.

Secondary: node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity existed elsewhere it would not be used.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the scheduler message changed to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, or a network policy rejection) on a re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would not be the root cause.

If kubectl or cluster tooling showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota, or affinity bug) would need to be investigated.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes were found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod affinity rules were recently changed to exclude them, the primary cause would shift to an affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run passes without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent pod creation that temporarily exhausted slots) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the shared scheduling layer would not be the cause and the diagnosis would need to be localized to the runtime probe specifically.
